title: Vault withdrawal
summary: State ordering, caller authorization and unchecked calls in a minimal asset vault.
caveat: Three planted patterns. This teaching fixture is not an independent accuracy benchmark.

candidates.title: External call before balance update
candidates.rationale: external call before state update -> possible REENTRANCY
candidates.recommendation: Apply checks-effects-interactions: update state BEFORE the external call, or use OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard.

candidates.title: tx.origin authorization
candidates.recommendation: Use msg.sender for authorization; tx.origin is phishable.

candidates.title: Unchecked low-level call
candidates.recommendation: Capture and check the boolean: (bool ok, ) = ...; require(ok);.

limitations: Regex baseline only: source has not been compiled; imports and dependencies are not resolved.
Source-bound evidence proves a location, not exploitability or semantic correctness.
Comments, formatting, naming and function-scope heuristics can cause false positives and misses.

candidates.recommendation: Inspect both sides of the callback; do not infer that an external victim is vulnerable.

title: Delegated execution
summary: Delegatecall and ownership mutation as execution-authority review candidates.
caveat: Original preserved unchanged. It contains compiler-incompatible syntax; no compilation is claimed.

candidates.title: Delegatecall requires review
candidates.rationale: A delegatecall is present. The rule does not establish that its target is attacker-controlled.
candidates.recommendation: Trace target control, upgrade authorization and storage compatibility before adjudication.

candidates.title: Ownership change requires review
candidates.rationale: function 'pwn' changes ownership with no access control
candidates.recommendation: Restrict state-changing/ownership functions with an access-control modifier (e.g. OpenZeppelin onlyOwner/RBAC).

title: Block-data guessing game
summary: Randomness assumptions and conditional asset payouts.
caveat: The asset-transfer rule also fires on a conditional payout: an example requiring false-positive review.

candidates.title: Block-data randomness candidate
candidates.rationale: Block data occurs in a contract containing randomness-related terms; data flow is unverified.
candidates.recommendation: Trace the randomness source and adversarial influence over outcomes and asset payouts.

candidates.title: Asset transfer requires review
candidates.rationale: A transfer occurs without a guard recognized by the rule. Legitimate payouts may match.
candidates.recommendation: Review intended permissions, recipient selection, preconditions and business invariants.

title: Two-player parity game
summary: Public player choices and predictable economic outcomes.
caveat: Missing compiler pragma is retained. No bytecode, compiler or execution test has been performed.

candidates.title: Predictable game outcome
candidates.rationale: winner is derived from player-supplied parity -> predictable game outcome
candidates.recommendation: The second player can read the first player's number on-chain and pick a winning parity. Use commit-reveal so choices are hidden until locked in.

candidates.title: Missing compiler pragma
candidates.rationale: missing Solidity compiler pragma -> compiler version is not pinned
candidates.recommendation: Add a pinned pragma, e.g. `pragma solidity 0.8.24;`, so the contract cannot be compiled with an unexpected/older compiler.
